fact: HMS Hood was the largest warship in the world at the time of her sinking
source: HMS Hood Association / National Museum of the Royal Navy

fact: Hood's deck armor was known to be inadequate against modern plunging shellfire
source: The Battlecruiser HMS Hood: An Illustrated Biography, Bruce Taylor (2005)

fact: Hood was sent to intercept Bismarck in the Denmark Strait
source: Bismarck: The Final Days of Germany's Greatest Battleship, Niklas Zetterling & Michael Tamelander (2009)

fact: A shell penetrated Hood's deck and detonated her aft magazines, causing the explosion
source: Board of Enquiry into the Loss of HMS Hood, 1941 (Admiralty records)

fact: Only 3 men survived out of a crew of 1,415
source: HMS Hood Association crew records; widely documented in official Royal Navy history

fact: Hood's planned major refit/reconstruction was postponed multiple times before the war
source: The Battlecruiser HMS Hood: An Illustrated Biography, Bruce Taylor (2005)
